name: – Andrzej Halicki – § 3 – Am 6
title: REPORT on the Council position on Draft amending budget No 3/2026 of the European Union for the financial year 2026 – Adjustments in expenditure, update of revenues and other technical updates
part_text: 3. Reiterates its firm opposition to the introduction of any new Union own resources; recalls that, in its annual report concerning the 2025 financial year, the European Court of Auditors highlights the increase in Union debt, with outstanding debt rising by more than 20 % in 2025 to reach EUR 738,9 billion and potentially approaching EUR 1 000 billion by 2027; notes that interest payments alone on NextGenerationEU non-repayable support could amount to nearly EUR 93 billion over the 2028–2034 period, while expected borrowing costs under the current multiannual financial framework remain twice as high as initially estimated; deplores the fact that the Commission has still not published a comprehensive strategy for repaying this debt by 2058, despite proposing to allocate EUR 24 billion annually to interest payments and principal repayments; rejects any attempt to use the consequences of this growing indebtedness as a pretext for introducing new European taxes or transferring national tax revenues to the Union budget; stresses that it would be irresponsible to place the burden of an insufficiently controlled borrowing policy on taxpayers, businesses and future generations; calls, therefore, for the sustainability of Union finances to be ensured primarily through strict budgetary discipline, reductions in expenditure in areas falling outside the scope of the Treaties, as well as to ideologically driven or non-essential expenditure, strengthened controls and the establishment of a credible and transparent debt repayment strategy, rather than through the introduction of new own resources;
